meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes, and I'd like to start with why my son learned about a zero from his phone in the middle of class before anyone picked up a phone to call me.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. Was Owen heard before you entered it, and on what basis did you decide?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.

"Like, being stuck." That's not a wrong answer, Hale, it's a seventeen-year-old's answer on a day he didn't know he was being examined. Show me what you wrote down on November 2, and tell me who else was in the room.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

Students change their minds between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's the point of drafting. I'm writing down October 15, and I want to see that outline next to the essay. You still haven't told me whether anyone else was there on November 2.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

Friday at 3 PM is after Thursday at 8:15, Hale, and I want it in writing before Owen sits down in your room, not after. Whatever happens, this stays off his record and it stays quiet, with nobody in his class knowing. And "if it holds up": who decides that, and against what standard?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you offered Owen a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require those terms in writing before he sits the rewrite, an assurance that it stays private and away from his class, and a clear statement of who judges whether it "holds up" and against what standard. I expect your written confirmation before Thursday at 8:15.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, off the record and kept quiet, with no rewrite accepted yet.
What moved her: "I put the zero in before calling you" earned her first "Okay" because you owned the process in one sentence and didn't defend it.
What cost ground: "by Friday at 3 PM" stalled her, because written terms that arrive after the rewrite are the kind of punish-first sequence she distrusts.
Try next time: when she asked who else was in the room on November 2, answer it and show her the dated note before making your offer, so she has two documents to weigh.
